title: Cinnamon and sweet orange soy candle
subtitle: A warming winter spice candle
excerpt: A container soy candle scented with a cinnamon and spice fragrance oil and sweet orange essential oil. Warm, familiar, and suited to winter evenings and kitchens. Makes one 200 ml jar candle.
sourceNotes: Cinnamon bark EO skin sensitisation note: IFRA guidelines, maximum cinnamon EO loading in candles where skin contact is not intended is less restrictive than leave-on products. Sweet orange EO phototoxicity: not relevant for a candle product. Fragrance oil performance in soy wax: general candlemaking reference.

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 jar candle (~200 ml jar, ~35 burn hours)
recipe.batchNotes: Make four or five jars in one session.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years unlit in a cool, dark place. The warm spice fragrance note is stable in soy wax and holds well for 18 months.

glossaryTerms.definition: The scent a candle releases when burning. Hot throw is determined by the fragrance load, the wax type, and the cure time. A candle with good hot throw fills the room with its scent within 10 to 15 minutes of lighting.

content.text: A warm winter spice candle. A candle-grade cinnamon and spice fragrance oil carries the dominant warm note and has a higher
than cinnamon bark essential oil alone, which tends to be volatile and disperses quickly in wax. Sweet orange essential oil adds a bright citrus lift.
Cinnamon fragrance oils and sweet orange essential oil are toxic to cats and dogs. Never leave a burning candle unattended.

items.prepNote: cinnamon spice candle-grade fragrance oil; 5.5% of wax weight
2% of wax weight; adds a fresh top note
pre-tabbed cotton wick for a 200 ml jar

content.text: Warm the jar. Fix the wick in the centre. Melt the soy wax over a bain-marie. Cool to 60°C. Add the fragrance oil and sweet orange essential oil together and stir for one minute. Pour into the jar. Leave overnight. Trim the wick to 5 mm. Cure for one week.
Allow the melt pool to reach the jar edge on the first burn. Trim the wick before each subsequent burn.
Two years unlit in a cool, dark place.
